summary: Backend-only (CLI tool) retest of backend/tools/reset_student_data.py. Ran serially (-n 0) only against isolated DBs tejas_isolated_reset144 and tejas_isolated_restore144, with an in-memory FakeStore and a fake tejas_storage module. No real storage PUT, no owner login, no secrets printed, and no reset run against the customer DB. Test file extended from 40 to 64 cases, with 0 xfail markers left. The 4 former strict xfails are now ordinary tests and all pass: (1) orphan scope protects owner/staff rows; (2) restore keeps raw BSON field order; (3) a missing or re-approved part is blocked; (4) the manifest records indexes in the new m.collections[name] shape. Results were 62/64 passing in each of 3 consecutive runs, with no flaky tests (the threaded parallel-resumer tests were stable). The 2 failures are one real defect: apply() accepts any receipt phase that isn't 'complete', so a receipt in a foreign phase that still holds a valid protected_sha256 (e.g. 'restored' or 'aborted') is re-applied and student data is deleted again. Verified: (a) CLI adapter: put_object(path, blob, 'application/gzip') returns a str, which is wrapped as {'path': str}; the path is tejas/student-reset-backups/<owner_id>/<uuid4>.jsonl.gz, a private path rather than a URL. Every PUT is followed by an uncached request('GET') of the same path. A 404 during apply fails closed. Apply makes no PUTs. Printed output contains no path, email or phone. (b) Orphan scope: owner, admin and reviewer rows, plus rows of a phone-profile reviewer, that share an orphan attempt id are retained byte-identical. This covers reviews, ledgers (including id == orphan id), jobs, cohort entries, question reports, score versions and sessions. Anonymous rows are deleted. A report job of an unlinked job-only user is captured; unlinked/shared AI jobs are retained. (c) Backup and restore: shadow restore recreates the options of every collection (including an empty collection with validator + collation), the compound unique and TTL indexes with key ORDER, and the raw rows. Result: 0 of 322 docs differ at raw BSON level, including 160 type-stress docs with shuffled field order. Manifest shape per collection is {options, type, indexes, records, sha256}, and I recomputed the stream sha independently. Receipt parts_hash, collections_hash and plan_hash match. A missing part that is re-approved is blocked. Deep tampers with all receipt hashes recomputed are also blocked: dropped part, dropped part plus metadata, wrong target digest, target missing from a forged part, duplicate part, wrong collection count, wrong sha. None of these deleted anything. (d) Lease: a future lease blocks both prepared and applying resumers until it expires on the DB clock. A nested rival resumer is blocked and performs 0 deletes. The lease is never refreshed (same token and deadline on every batch). With 4 threaded resumers (prepared and applying), exactly one writer runs. An expired or stolen lease stops the next batch. Lease expiry before the final check stops finalization. The finally block releases the lease after a handled failure, so resume can start immediately, and it does not clear a foreign holder's lease. A lost CAS or rival lease fails before deletion. All old guard, drift, tamper, partial-crash and resume tests still pass.

critical.issue: apply() only short-circuits on phase=='complete'. The CAS filter uses {'phase': receipt['phase']}, which accepts ANY phase. A receipt in a foreign or terminal phase that still has protected_sha256 (e.g. 'restored' after an operator restore, or 'aborted') passes the CAS, is flipped to 'applying', and student data is deleted again. Reproduced 3/3 runs: test_foreign_phase_or_lost_cas_fails_before_deletion[restored_with_valid_hash] and [aborted_with_valid_hash].

minor.issue: A foreign phase WITHOUT protected_sha256 (e.g. 'cancelled') fails closed, but only by accident: the CAS first rewrites the receipt to phase='applying' with protected_sha256=None. Every later resume then fails with 'Protected data changed', and the receipt's original phase is lost.

This was observed in the code review but not asserted by any test. The first tejas_jobs branch, payload.attempt_id IN attempts AND user_id NOT IN protected, has no kind filter. A shared ai_solution/content job whose payload references a student attempt (and which has no staff user_id) would be deleted. Confirm whether this is intended.

action_items: In apply(): fail closed unless receipt['phase'] in ('prepared','applying'), before verified_manifest and before the CAS. Make the CAS filter {'phase': {'$in': ['prepared','applying']}} AND require the phase read earlier (or pin the exact phase) so a foreign phase can never become 'applying'. Then rerun the suite; the 2 failing parametrized cases must pass.
Optional: add a kind filter (grade/report/cohort) to the tejas_jobs payload.attempt_id branch, or document that any non-staff job referencing a student attempt is personal.
critical_code_review_comments: The lease is never refreshed, by design. A very large apply that takes more than 300s will stop with 'lease expired' and must be resumed; tell the operator about this.
The binding is sha256(MONGO_URL + DB_NAME). If MONGO_URL credentials are rotated between prepare and apply, apply will refuse, which fails safe; tell the deployer about this.
Hypothetical views were not tested (none exist in the real DB). list_indexes on a view would raise in prepare, which fails closed.
Writer quiescence is still an operator flag (--writers-paused). It is not automatic, which is correctly not claimed.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_iter144_student_reset.py (test-only: removed 4 xfails; new index-metadata shape; CLI fake-adapter wiring test; scope, manifest and lease tests; seed adds 160 type-stress docs, an empty validated collection, compound unique/TTL indexes, unlinked job-only user)

success_rate.backend: 62/64 (96.9%) in each of 3 runs; both failures are the same phase-gate defect

seed_data_creation: Synthetic qa144-* data only, inside tejas_isolated_reset144 and tejas_isolated_restore144. Each DB is dropped once at session start and once at end. Between tests, data is wiped with delete_many. Teardown proof after the runs: neither isolated DB is in list_database_names; the customer DB has 0 qa144 rows and 0 tejas_student_resets receipts; its collection set and estimated counts are unchanged (REAL_DB_COUNTS_UNCHANGED True); mongod ping ok. mongod FD limit is soft 65536.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter144_student_reset.py -q -n 0 (MUST use -n 0, since there is one shared isolated DB; a run takes about 11s). restore_shadow() requires a fresh shadow DB: only the e2e test creates collections there, so do not add another test that creates shadow collections. TTL index expireAfterSeconds is 10 years so the TTL monitor never fires on 2026 seed dates. The CLI test monkeypatches sys.modules['tejas_storage'], R.MongoClient (which always returns TEST_DB) and ADMIN_EMAIL (in-process only). The only expected failures before the fix are the 2 foreign-phase cases.
rca of the issue: apply() reads the receipt, returns early only on 'complete', and computes protection = protected_fingerprint() if phase=='prepared' else receipt.get('protected_sha256'). The CAS then matches {'_id', 'phase': receipt['phase'], lease expired}. Any other phase with a stored protected_sha256 therefore passes every gate and deletes. Repro: prepare, then $set phase='restored' and protected_sha256=<current fingerprint>, then apply returns 'complete' and the targets are deleted. Mitigation: whitelist the phases.
